_description: Task13 DRIFT field, FINE transcription -- the 0.1mm grid used for BOTH the near-field solve and the final stitched volume, for the 5x5 LArPix v2a tile at the true 4.4mm pitch. The coarse sibling (example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_task13_coarse.json) is the 0.22mm far-field grid. NOTHING IS SNAPPED HERE, which is the opposite of the coarse file: at 0.1mm every true design length is an exact whole number of cells -- pixelSize 3.5 -> 35 cells, pixelGap 0.9 -> 9, chamfer_r 0.7 -> 7 (via int(round()) in the generator; 0.7/0.1 is 6.999999999999999 in binary float, so the rounding is load-bearing). The coarse file carries the snapped 3.52 / 0.88 / 0.66 with the design values preserved as _design_* keys; here the values ARE the design values. PITCH: 3.5 + 0.9 = 4.4mm = 44 fine cells and 20 coarse cells of 0.22mm. hybrid_iterate.py _cells() requires the transverse extent to be a WHOLE number of cells and raises otherwise. PIXEL PLANE LOW EDGE 9.9 IS LOAD-BEARING: 9.9mm is 99 fine cells AND 45 coarse cells of 0.22mm, so the pad plane lands on a real node of BOTH grids. Moving it breaks that co-location. (The generator reads this key with int(), not int(round()) -- gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.py:474 -- so never reason about it in decimal; 9.9/0.1 is exactly 99.0 and 9.9/0.22 exactly 45.0 in binary float, but neighbouring values are not so lucky.) DEPTH: driftZDepth 79.15 is the electron launch node, deliberately NOT rounded to 79.2. The cathode sits on the domain's last plane at ceil(79.15/0.22) = 360 coarse cells = 79.2mm, which is 792 fine cells exactly, so both grids close on the same physical cathode; the launch node itself does not land on that grounded plane, which is the point. CATHODE FORMULA, so the value can be recomputed by hand when the drift length or the bulk field changes: CathodePotential = -BulkField * (driftZDepth - pixelPlaneLowEdgePosition). The value is maintained BY HAND on purpose, so the bulk field stays a visible, editable number rather than a derived one. CathodePotential -3878 preserves the design FIELD across the retarget: the original -8400 over the old 159.9 - 9.9 = 150.0mm is exactly 56.0 V/mm (560 V/cm), and 56.0 * (79.15 - 9.9) = 3878.0 V reproduces it here. Leaving -8400 would have given 121.3 V/mm. The FIELD is what is preserved, not the voltage, because velo derives the mobility from E through a nonlinear LAr parameterisation -- at 121 V/mm the drift velocity is not simply doubled and the paths stop being comparable to production. The SAME voltage is applied on the coarse and the fine grid, deliberately: it is a boundary condition. The ACHIEVED field differs slightly between them because the laminate discretises differently -- coarse pad top 10.56mm (index 48 at 0.22mm: pp_loweredge 45 plus pp_width 3, from padThickness and FR4Thickness 0.4mm each rounding to 2 cells) against fine 10.0mm (index 100, pp_width 1), giving 3878/68.64 = 56.498 V/mm coarse against 3878/69.20 = 56.040 V/mm fine, a spread of 0.8%. That is expected and is the same class of error as the coarse pad-area snap; do NOT compensate for it with different voltages. TILE SIZE: Npixels 5, i.e. a 5x5 pad tile at the 4.4mm pitch = 22.0mm transverse for the weighting probe; the DRIFT field is one periodic tile, so Npixels does not size this file's domain. GridPotential does NOT enter the cathode calculation: the shield grid has holes and is transparent at the tile centre, so it is not an equipotential plane terminating the field. The bulk field is set by the CATHODE against the PIXEL PLANE at 0 V. GridPotential instead sets the collection field between the grid and the pads.
